transcript:
Meeting header:
2026-05-29 15:00 PDT | Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Alex Moreno (Redwood AE), Maya Sato (Redwood SE), Kenji Rao (Redwood CS), Dr. Lin Chen (Ambercliff CTO), Priya Nair (Ambercliff Head of ML), Jordan Ellis (Ambercliff Procurement), Sam Ortiz (Ambercliff SRE)

--- Auto Summary (auto-gen, may be noisy):
Ambercliff checking on renewal timing, wants additional capacity and two new regions (eu-west, apac-east). Discussed private VPC vs dedicated pools, KMS needs, and latency targets for inference. Redwood to share pricing and security docs and run perf benchmarks.

--- Transcript body:
[00:00] Alex (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick rollcall, then we'll jump into the uplift numbers and the VPC options. How's everyone doing?
[00:08] Dr. Lin (CTO): Doing well, thanks. Busy week but glad we could get this on the calendar.
[00:12] Priya (Head of ML): Hi all. We just finished a run on staging, saw a lot of tail latency spikes which is why capacity + region matters.
[00:20] Maya (Redwood SE): Thanks Priya, can you share rough numbers? Is it p99 spikes or more like p95?
[00:24] Priya: It's around p99, so like 700 to 1,200ms on some long prompt workloads, and that kills a few user flows.
[00:31] Alex: Got it. We're expecting that with cross-region traffic if things aren't pinned. The uplift we're talking about would give you capacity headroom and also let us deploy eu-west and apac-east endpoints to reduce RTT.
[00:41] Jordan (Procurement): Quick question on timing — we need contract terms by mid-June to sync with finance for the PO. Is that feasible?
[00:47] Alex: We can certainly aim for that. We'll send an updated term sheet and a pricing band by June 2.
[00:52] Sam (SRE): For the private option, we need to understand the VPC peering and egress patterns. Also does Redwood support customer-managed KMS?
[00:59] Maya: Yes, customer-managed KMS is supported for Private; we have KMS/HSM integrations and an on-prem connector for the HSM flow. We'll share the KMS notes. (murmur) the only caveat is for dedicated hosted we have a managed KMS option with BYOK as well.
[01:12] Dr. Lin: Important for us — the sample data classifies as regulated, so we need audit logs and key rotation policies visible in the SSO flow.
[01:19] Maya: Absolutely, audit logs are available and RBAC ties into SAML SSO. We'll include sample audit exports in the security pack.
[01:26] Priya: On the perf side, we want to validate quantization profiles, batching, and KV cache behavior — we've seen weirdness where the K V cash (sic) looked like dropped keys in a small-scale run.
[01:36] Maya: Noted, we sometimes see the transcription of that as K V cash in our notes too — it's KV cache. We can run a KV cache sanity test during the perf run.
[01:43] Alex: For capacity sizing, can you share typical tokens/sec and concurrency targets? We had a note from last quarter but want to confirm.
[01:50] Priya: OK, baseline is 6k tokens/sec across inference, with peaks up to 18k during campaign bursts. Concurrency target is 120 concurrent sessions with 1.2k token window average.
[02:02] Maya: That lines up with a 3x uplift recommendation we shared in the spreadsheet. If you commit to dedicated capacity we can guarantee throughput and prioritize scheduling to hit p95/p99 SLOs.
[02:13] Dr. Lin: What's the latency tradeoff if we push quantization and higher batching to save cost? We cannot exceed 500ms median for critical flows.
[02:21] Maya: With careful batch sizing (small per-request windows) and prefix caching you can keep medians under 350ms on dedicated GPUs. Quantization helps cost but can add a small delta; we'll recommend a quant profile that preserves quality.
[02:33] Priya: Any model variants we should consider? We currently run a 13B open model, thinking about switching to a quantized 13B plus a fallback 7B for low-cost paths.
[02:42] Alex: We often recommend a weighted routing policy — primary 13B quantized for quality, fallback 7B for low-cost non-critical paths. The smart routing can do region-aware fallbacks too.
[02:51] Jordan: On billing — if we go with a committed capacity, how does overage work? Also any minimum term?
[02:57] Alex: Standard is monthly committed units with a 12-month term for best pricing. Overage is billed at a lower reserved overage rate if within 10% buffer, otherwise on-demand rates apply. We'll put exact numbers in the term sheet.
[03:09] Sam: For the VPC, do we need an open port to Redwood control plane? Our security wants to avoid inbound rules as much as possible.
[03:16] Maya: For Private, the control-plane calls are outbound from your VPC to Redwood endpoints; we can support a VPN or private link. We'll provide a diagram.
[03:23] Dr. Lin: Did you mention SOC two and ISO stuff? We need evidence for our auditors — also pen-test reports.
[03:28] Kenji (CS): Yes, SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 attestations, plus a redacted pen test summary — we'll include all in the pack. There may be some PII redactions but enough for audit.
[03:37] Priya: Great. Regarding the perf test, we want two days: day one cold start and KV cache warmup, day two steady-state throughput with synthetic traffic. Can Redwood provision a dedicated pool for that week?
[03:48] Maya: We can reserve a small dedicated pool for the benchmark. We'll need a signed scoping doc and window. Alex, can we confirm week of June 7?
[03:56] Alex: Yes, we'll aim for June 7-8. I'll coordinate with Kenji to lock capacity.
[04:01] Priya: Also want to validate model rollout behavior — can we do a canary swap during the second day's test?
[04:06] Maya: Yes, canary deploys are supported; we can do A/B routing and measure quality regressions. We'll include automatic fallback to previous model in the policy.
[04:14] Dr. Lin: On data residency: EU data must not leave region. For APAC we need egress auditing. Is there a way to pin endpoints?
[04:21] Alex: Yes, with regional endpoints we can ensure processing happens in-region; for private deployment we can enforce strict routing policies. We'll detail residency controls in the VPC guide.
[04:29] Jordan: From procurement: do you offer a 30-day invoice? Our standard is 30 nett but we need to confirm payment terms for new committed spend.
[04:35] Alex: Standard is 30 days, but for enterprise we can negotiate 45 or net-60 on request — that would be part of the commercial discussions.
[04:43] Sam: One more SRE question — how are drain/failover handled when a region loses capacity? We need graceful degradation and fallback.
[04:50] Maya: Smart routing handles capacity-based fallback to compatible model variants in other regions. There is also a circuit-breaker policy for graceful degradation and throttling to keep critical flows online. We'll share our runbook.
[05:01] [crosstalk] Dr. Lin: OK that sounds good.
[05:04] Alex: Quick reprioritization: We'll send price + term sheet, security pack, and VPC guide; we will schedule the perf test tentatively for June 7-8 pending the scoping signoff. Anything else?
[05:14] Priya: Can you also include a sample prompt set and the scoring rubric you use for quality regression alerts?
[05:19] Maya: Yep, quality monitoring and eval rubric will be part of the Optimize suggestions. We'll attach a sample prompt set.
[05:25] Jordan: If you can get me a draft PO link and exact pricing, I can move finance faster.
[05:30] Alex: Understood, we'll prioritize the pricing band in the term sheet.
[05:33] Dr. Lin: Timeline wise, we need private VPC by end of Q3 for a regulated launch. That gives us runway.
[05:40] Alex: Noted. We'll map milestones in the follow-up mail.
[05:44] [long pause/typing sounds]
[05:50] Maya: One note — there are small model behaviour differences when using aggressive quant profiles; we'll recommend a test across 5 prompts that are sensitive to hallucination.
[05:59] Priya: Good, add safety/quality checks in the perf plan.
[06:03] Alex: Alright, final recap and owners: Alex will output pricing and target Po by 6/2, Maya sends security pack by 6/1, Kenji VPC/KMS by 6/3, and we'll tentatively book June 7-8 perf windows.
[06:16] Dr. Lin: Thanks everyone.
[06:18] Jordan: Thanks.
[06:20] Alex: Thanks, talk soon.

--- End of transcript

Notes: Transcript contains some auto-caption errors and minor speaker mislabels; refer to attached recording for exact timing. References to 'K V cash' are transcription artifacts for 'KV cache'.
